_comment: OUT-OF-SCOPE pret labels: things this port is NOT going to translate, excluded
from the completeness scores in docs/translation_progress.md so that report says
what still needs WRITING rather than counting work nobody will ever do.
MAINTAINER-CONTROLLED. An agent MUST NOT add an entry here to make its own
numbers look better - that is the same failure mode CLAUDE.md's rules about the
pret_label_allowlist exist to prevent. Entries are added only when the maintainer
says so, and each one states WHY the label is unportable rather than merely unported.
'Unused in pret' is NOT a reason to exclude. Maintainer direction 2026-08-23:
unused pret routines get ported anyway when they are genuinely portable in this
framework, for completeness and bug compatibility, even if they stay unlinked -
uncalled code does not run, so it carries no runtime risk. GetwMoves and
OverwritewMoves were ported on exactly that basis, not excluded.
Excluded labels are still reported, in their own section, so the exclusion is
visible and auditable instead of silently shrinking the denominator.

home/pikachu_cries.asm.reason: The Game Boy's 1-bit wave-channel bit-bang loop for Pikachu's digitized voice. PlayPikachuPCM streams samples by writing rAUD3LEVEL in a tight timing loop; LoadNextSoundClipSample and PlaySoundClipSample are its inner helpers. The port cannot host this even in principle: its APU is virtual, and the per-device shims read rAUD3LEVEL ONCE PER audio_tick (src/audio/opl_shim.asm:707, src/audio/tandy_shim.asm:492), so a literal translation would emit silence rather than sound. The data model diverges too - tools/audio/gen_pika_pcm.py has already low-pass-filtered and decimated pret's 1-bit streams to 8-bit PCM. The cry itself IS implemented, faithfully and at its correct pret path: pret moved PlayPikachuSoundClip into audio/pikachu_pcm.asm (upstream bd1b695b) and the port mirrors it there, dispatching to the Sound Blaster DSP or the PC-speaker PWM player. src/audio/sb_pcm.asm:25 already carries the DEVIATION{class=HAL} for this replacement. Maintainer decision 2026-08-23.

home/timer.asm.reason: The Game Boy's timer-interrupt vector. Timer is not a routine anything calls: its sole reference in pret is home/header.asm:57 `jp Timer` at the $0050 hardware vector, and its entire body is `reti` under pret's own comment, "timer interrupt is apparently not invoked anyway" - the ROM never enables IE bit 2, so it does not run even on hardware. The port has no GB interrupt-vector table to hang it on: its timing is a native PIT channel-0 ISR installed by pit_init (dos_port/boot/entry.asm, divisor from -D PIT_DIVISOR, see boot/timing.asm), which is the DOS host's own interrupt path and shares nothing with the GB's. There is therefore no site at which a translated `reti` could be placed and nothing that would reach it. This is exclusion in the strict sense the header requires - unportable in this framework, not merely unported - and it is NOT the disallowed 'unused in pret' rationale: the bar those routines clear (GetwMoves, OverwritewMoves) is being genuinely portable, which a hardware interrupt vector on absent hardware is not. Maintainer decision 2026-08-23.

engine/movie/intro_yellow.asm.reason: SM83 ROM bankswitching helpers for bank $3E. The Game Boy intro copies and fills memory across bank boundaries via these routines; in the port's flat 32-bit protected mode, all ROM/VRAM is directly addressable and memory operations use standard flat copy/fill without bank switching. Maintainer decision 2026-08-26.

engine/movie/title.asm.reason: The title screen's 1-bit wave-channel timer bit-bang trigger for Pikachu's title cry. In the port, Pikachu PCM is handled via audio/pikachu_pcm.asm and the Sound Blaster DSP / PC-speaker PWM HAL (src/audio/sb_pcm.asm). Maintainer decision 2026-08-26.

home/header.asm.reason: Game Boy RST vectors ($0000-$0038), hardware interrupt vectors ($0040 VBlank, $0048 LCDC, $0050 Timer, $0058 Serial, $0060 Joypad) and the cartridge header/entry at $0100 (Start: nop; jp _Start; ds $0150). The port boots as a DOS MZ protected-mode program via boot/entry.asm (CWSDPMI, pit_init, setup_flat_access, vga_base/ds_base), not as a GB ROM, so there is no GB vector table to host these vectors and no $0100 header to patch with rgbfix. Start is the only named label in the file; the rst/interrupt stubs are section vectors. Maintainer decision 2026-08-30 per user request to blacklist header.asm.
